abstract: Achieving a balance between recommending popular items and long-tail items has consistently posed a challenge in the field of recommendation systems. Traditional recommendation algorithms often exhibit a bias towards recommending popular items, resulting in limited exposure for long-tail items. To address this issue, our study introduces an innovative recommendation algorithm based on graph contrastive learning. This algorithm incorporates a dual-view learning mechanism with the objective of increasing the exposure of long-tail items while ensuring the accuracy of recommendations. Two distinct views are generated: one captures in-depth information of long-tail nodes through random walk strategies, while the other utilizes Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to acquire node importance and contextual information. By means of contrastive learning with these two views, our model attains comprehensive node representations. The study strives to achieve a balanced learning process between long-tail and high-frequency nodes. Experimental results conducted on multiple recommendation system datasets substantiate that our approach significantly enhances the exposure of long-tail items compared to existing recommendation algorithms, while maintaining high accuracy and recall in recommendations. This research attests that the contrastive learning framework provides an effective strategy for addressing the long-tail recommendation problem.

articleTitle: Study on Intelligent Data Assimilation Method Based on Equivalent-Weights Particle Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: In the study of ocean dynamics, the particle filter method has gradually become a research hotspot in the field of data assimilation due to its advantages in nonlinear and non-Gaussian systems. At present, the most direct sources of information on marine environmental elements are buoys and autonomous unmanned observation platforms, but the observation data obtained by these two methods are sparse and unevenly distributed. Therefore, how to use the particle filter method to organically integrate the sparse and unevenly distributed observation data with the ocean numerical model to improve the accuracy of analysis and forecasting of marine environmental elements is a difficult problem that needs to be solved urgently. Based on the equivalent-weights particle filter method and the characteristics of the particle swarm optimization algorithm that can search for the global optimal solution, this paper studies and analyzes the defects of the traditional equivalent-weights particle filter method that relies on future observation information to adjust the particles, and proposes an equivalent-weights particle filter assimilation method based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm. The proposed method is experimentally verified for sparse and unevenly distributed marine environmental observation data combined with regional ocean numerical models.

articleTitle: Precision Diabetes Risk Assessment: A Feature Grouping Approach to Model Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is emerging as a global health crisis, with increasing prevalence rates that underscore the critical need for early intervention strategies. Traditional diabetes prediction models, however, have a common limitation: they often overlook the nuanced individual characteristics of patients, opting instead for a one-size-fits-all approach to data training. In a departure from these conventional methodologies, our study introduces an innovative approach that leverages the power of feature grouping to enhance predictive accuracy. We have developed a tailored prediction model for each distinct feature group, demonstrating a more refined understanding of patient heterogeneity. Our dataset, sourced from comprehensive health examinations conducted at Hospital X in 2022, was meticulously curated using three feature selection techniques: mutual information, correlation analysis, and recursive feature elimination. These methods were employed to distill a set of pivotal features, which subsequently informed the stratification of the dataset. The efficacy of our models was rigorously assessed through a suite of performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Our comparative analysis revealed that the implementation of feature-based grouping strategies led to a marked enhancement in all evaluated metrics, signifying an overall improvement in predictive performance. The findings of this study corroborate the superior predictive capabilities of our proposed model, which harnesses the nuances of important feature grouping. This model not only demonstrates a heightened accuracy in diabetes prediction but also holds significant potential to facilitate timely clinical diagnosis, thereby enhancing preventive healthcare measures for diabetic patients.

articleTitle: Implementing Digital Recognition Based on Transmissive Optical Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Optical Neural Networks (ONNs) have attracted great attention from both academia and industry due to their distinct advantages in power consumption, parallelism, and computational speed. This paper presents a novel ONN system that not only reduces the distances between system components but also enhances network accuracy. By employing fully transmissive optical devices, such as transmissive spatial light modulators, the system utilizes a single optical axis for light propagation. A micro-lens array (MLA) is used to enlarge the input optical field, where the relation between the number of micro-lenses in this MLA and the accuracy of this ONN have been investigated. Moreover, the number of micro-lenses has been optimized according above relationship. Meanwhile, the relation between the important parameters, such as the position and the size, of a detection unit and the accuracy of this ONN has been studied. Using the MNIST handwritten digit dataset as a test case, this ONN achieved an accuracy rate to 96.1%. Finally, this architecture is validated by experiment, which show a great accuracy for digital recognition.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Knowledge Graphs for Optical Communication Networks and Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: This research focuses on the field of optical communication networks and equipment, aiming to construct a comprehensive knowledge graph. By thoroughly analyzing the structural characteristics of optical communication networks and the related data of optoelectronic devices, this paper initially organizes and defines a well-established ontology conceptual system. Building on this foundation, advanced tools such as LangChain and the ontology construction software Protégé are utilized for meticulous modeling, successfully establishing the ontology model of the knowledge graph for optical communication networks and equipment. To achieve efficient management and application of the knowledge graph, Neo4j graph database is selected for storage, querying, and other operations. The constructed knowledge graph not only unveils the complex architectures and categorical relationships within optical communication networks and equipment but also provides robust data support and decision-making foundations for areas such as intelligent operation and maintenance, equipment installation, and network construction, significantly advancing the intelligent development of the optical communication field.

articleTitle: Research on Event Driven Dynamic Graph Processing System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Dynamic graph processing is crucial in many applications such as anomaly detection, targeted advertising, financial fraud detection, and social network analysis. In view of the problem of a large number of repeated calculations in the incremental graph calculation process of the existing dynamic graph system, and the performance of the synchronous batch processing algorithm on the graph computing system is limited by the random reading and writing of vertex value synchronization overhead, resulting in poor performance. To solve the problem of descent, an event-driven asynchronous execution algorithm model is proposed. This algorithm model can process vertices sequentially according to the dependency chain of the graph, and convert additions and deletions during the update process into events. By merging the events in the update, it ensures that each vertex is only accessed once during each update process. Based on this algorithm model, a dynamic graph processing system EDGraph is implemented. Experimental results show that compared with existing dynamic graph processing systems, EDGraph avoids repeated calculations of vertices and reduces the number of memory accesses. Its performance is 1.78 times (up to 2.06 times) higher than the current state-of-the-art incremental graph system.

articleTitle: Memento: A New Multithread Deterministic Replay Debugging Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: The multithread deterministic replay debugging is a foundation problem in concurrent software programing, analysis and testing. Since there are many non-deterministic factors, realizing multithread deterministic replay debugging have been a challenge. This paper proposes a new multithread deterministic replay debugging method Memento. The main contributions include: Firstly, in the replay framework, the record and replay functions are realized independently as a shared library, which can be loaded to GDB dynamically during running. That can greatly reduce the complex of using debugging. Secondly, for system calls, which is a kind of important non-deterministic factor, its record and replay are solved by dynamic code stub using GDB, then corresponding record log is optimized to reduce the size of log file. This method supports almost all system calls. Thirdly, for thread schedule, another kind of important non-deterministic factor, its record and replay are solved by transferring schedule to access order of shared memory, and then corresponding record log is also optimized to reduce the size of log file and improve the debugging performance. Memento has the features including without need of supporting of special hardware and programing language and modifying the OS kernel and codes. The experimental results show that our method not only provides correct record and replay functions, but also perform well on log file size and running time.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Bug Triage Representation and Classification Approaches from Canonical to Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Bug triage is the task of assigning newly reported bugs to the proper developers or team for resolution. This is a critical point in software maintenance as it directly influences the time and correct allocation that impact the efficiency and effectiveness of the software process. In a global aspect, the number of teams/developers is extensive, which brings a challenge for bug triage. Traditional approaches to assign bugs struggle with the complexity of the problem. This paper proposes a comparative assessment for different text representation combined with text classification approaches for automated bug report triage by incorporating Large Language Models (LLMs) into the classification pipeline to surpass the limitations of canonical methods. Traditional classification methods were compared with LLM-enhanced models across accuracy metric. The results demonstrate an improvement in triage accuracy when utilizing the fine-tuned LLM, highlighting their potential to provide developer-appropriate bug assignments.

articleTitle: Enhanced Soft Fault Diagnosis in DC-DC Converters Using Sparse Representation and Markov Transition Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Faults in DC-DC converters are a major cause of power electronics equipment breakdowns, often due to the malfunction of semiconductor devices caused by aging and temperature effects. Although multiple studies highlight the potential of image recognition for fault diagnosis in DC-DC converters, there is limited information on how these techniques mature over time. This research examines capacitor and inductor degeneration, represented by a decrease in capacitance (C) and inductance (L). A capacitor is considered to have failed when C decreases by 5%. Similarly, inductor failure is characterized by a 5% decrease in inductance (L). This paper proposes a model to diagnose and identify faults using a time series of DC-DC converter data as input. The model performs sparse representation to extract the feature and clean noise on the data before encoding the raw signal into a two-dimensional representation and performs recognition and classification by a deep convolutional neural network. Traditional methods often struggle with distinguishing subtle variations in signal patterns under different fault conditions. The proposed method achieved 100% accuracy in simulated data and 97.00% in experimental data. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in diagnosing faults in a buck DC-DC converter, as validated by both simulations and laboratory experiments.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap using Contrastive Learning and Semantic Consistency for Unsupervised Neural Machine Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: In Unsupervised Neural Machine Translation (UNMT) tasks, the lack of extensive parallel corpora makes it challenging for the model to directly optimize the correspondence between the source and target languages. UNMT models primarily rely on learning from monolingual data, making it difficult to fully capture cross-linguistic semantic alignment and consistency during training. Therefore, effectively enhancing semantic alignment between the source and target languages under unsupervised conditions has become a key challenge in the field of UNMT. To address this issue, this study proposes a semantic alignment and consistency enhancement mechanism based on contrastive learning, aiming to improve the model's ability to capture cross-lingual semantic differences by constructing an optimization objective focused on semantic consistency. The method utilizes a pretrained cross-lingual model to generate semantic embeddings for both the source and target languages, then designs a contrastive learning-based loss function that minimizes the semantic distance between correct translations and source sentences while increasing the semantic distance between incorrect translations and source sentences, thereby enhancing the model's performance in semantic consistency. The experiments validate the effectiveness and broad applicability of the semantic consistency optimization method based on contrastive learning, demonstrating great potential and advantages, especially in multilingual tasks of UNMT. The model achieved significant improvements in BLEU scores across various language pairs.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Text Categorization Model Based on Semanteme and Label Knowledge Guidance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Since electric power text has strong professional knowledge and industry characteristics, traditional text classification model has the problems of extracting features not accurate enough and neglecting domain knowledge guidance, this paper proposes a multi-label text classification model for electric power based on Semanteme and knowledge guidance. The text features are extracted using Bert pre-trained language model, the public semantics are extracted based on the text set corresponding to each label as the guiding information of the labeled text, and the label feature vectors are trained using graph-attention neural network to get the deep semantics of the labels. The label feature vectors are used as knowledge guides in classification to get the text features based on the label semantic attention, and finally they are fed into the multilayer perceptual machine to realize classification. The experiment proves that the method proposed in this paper obtains improvement in classification accuracy, F1 value and other selected indexes, which can effectively improve the performance of automatic power text classification.

articleTitle: MERCA: A Multi-Objective Optimization Traffic Light Control Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: In recent years, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has demonstrated significant capabilities in adjusting traffic signal timing. However, designing a multi-objective reward structure and addressing the issue of reward sparsity remain major challenges for DRL. In this paper, the authors propose a new reinforcement learning model architecture called MERCA (Multi-objective Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient) for multi-objective reward optimization. MERCA constructs corresponding critic for each optimization objective, and updates the critics based on the aggregated evaluation values of all objectives to achieve multi-objective optimization. To address the reward sparsity issue, this paper further investigates reward shaping methods. MERCA learns an intrinsic reward function in a completely self-supervised manner, in addition to the external reward, and maximizes the agent's performance through exploration-based rewards. The paper compares MERCA with other baseline models using the traffic simulator SUMO. The experimental results demonstrate that MERCA exhibits better performance in conventional traffic metrics and has faster learning speed for the intelligent agent.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network Focused on Structural Features for Link Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks (HGNNs) inherit some of the mechanisms of traditional graph neural networks, and are able to focus on graph structures that contain different types of nodes and edges, effectively embedding their structural and semantic features into node representations. Little work has investigated whether these capabilities play a critical utility in the problem of link prediction for heterogeneous graphs. In this paper, we target these issues by proposing Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network Focused on Structural Features (SFH4LP). Mean value aggregation is used to simplify the computation of neighbor aggregation, while centrality coding is added to complement node representation. In order to exploit the structural information of the graph more comprehensively, the model pays deep attention to the edges and spatial relationships in the metapaths. An improved self-attention mechanism based on Transformer is proposed to explore the information implied on the metapaths and achieve high-quality fusion of features from different metapaths to generate the final node representations. Experimental results on three heterogeneous graph datasets show that the model proposed in this paper outperforms existing baseline models in terms of the effectiveness of heterogeneous graph embedding, and exhibits good performance for the link prediction task.

articleTitle: Efficient Plug-and-Play Module for Transformer-Based 3D Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Video pose transformers (VPTs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in 3D human pose prediction. However, transformer-based architectures are often computationally intensive, leading to prolonged training times. To address this issue, we propose an efficient and plug-and-play module named the Adaptive Token Management (ATM), to prune and recover pose tokens, enabling high efficiency and accurate predictions within the VPTs framework. ATM consists of two key modules: the Dynamic Token Pruning (DTP) and the Lightweight Token Recovery (LTR). The DTP is presented for dynamic tokens pruning, where it determines the optimal number of representative tokens based on feature distribution and selects the representative tokens through a scoring mechanism. The LTR module, an optional lightweight module, is designed for tasks requiring the recovery of full-length tokens. It selects an appropriate full-length token as a learnable initialization token, utilizing attention mechanisms to restore spatio-temporal information. We conducted extensive experiments on the Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP datasets, demonstrating that our approach can enhance the efficiency of mainstream VPTs while maintaining prediction accuracy. The results show that, when using MixSTE as the underlying framework on the Human3.6M dataset, ATM accelerated training time per epoch, reduced FLOPs by over 40%, and decreased prediction error by 0.2.

articleTitle: Advances in Electronic Health Record Analysis for Diabetes Risk Prediction: A Machine Learning-Enhanced Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Background: Diabetes mellitus is a prevalent chronic condition with escalating global incidence, underscoring the urgency for efficient early detection and management strategies to ameliorate healthcare burdens and enhance patient quality of life. Methods: We conducted a systematic data processing pipeline on electronic health examination data, which included de-identification, imputation of missing data, and feature scaling. Feature selection was performed using Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) complemented by a literature review to identify the most informative predictors. We developed five machine learning models: Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and LightGBM (LGBM). Model performance was quantitatively assessed using a comprehensive set of metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC). The LGBM model, which demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy, was subjected to hyperparameter optimization and cross-validated on an independent public dataset to ensure its generalizability. Results: The initial evaluation of the LGBM model yielded an accuracy of 90.52%, precision of 89.06%, recall of 88.97%, F1-score of 88.67%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.965. After hyperparameter tuning, these metrics were further improved to 91.38% accuracy, 89.87% precision, 90.13% recall, 89.94% F1-score, and an AUC-ROC of 0.969. The model's predictive capabilities were corroborated through successful cross-validation on external datasets, indicating its robustness and reliability. Conclusion: The study presents a sophisticated diabetes prediction model leveraging machine learning algorithms on electronic health examination data. The model's superior predictive performance and validated generalizability suggest its potential as a valuable asset for healthcare providers, aiding in the early identification of diabetes risk, thereby facilitating more informed clinical decisions and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Intelligent Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment Model for Hemorrhagic Stroke using Ensemble Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Hemorrhagic stroke accounts for 10-15% of stroke cases, posing a significant burden on patients and society. This study aims to develop an intelligent clinical diagnosis and treatment model for hemorrhagic stroke by integrating statistical models and algorithms-Bayesian parameter-optimized logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost-with patient imaging data to improve treatment outcomes and prognosis accuracy. We utilized follow-up imaging data within 48 hours of hemorrhagic stroke onset to explore factors related to hematoma expansion risk. Feature engineering was performed using a random forest classifier for feature selection, followed by constructing logistic regression and random forest models optimized through Bayesian parameter search to predict hematoma expansion probabilities, evaluated with the Brier score. Additionally, we developed XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models to predict patients' 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores, analyzing the relationship between prognosis and factors such as personal history, disease history, treatment methods, and imaging features, with model performance compared using mean squared error (MSE). The results indicated that the random forest model was superior in predicting hematoma expansion risk, while the CatBoost model outperformed both XGBoost and LightGBM for 90-day mRS score prediction. Prognostic analysis revealed that hematoma volume, edema volume, and age positively influenced mRS scores, whereas a history of stroke did not significantly impact mRS scores. Continuous monitoring of hematoma and edema volumes, along with age considerations, is crucial for effective patient management.

articleTitle: Analysis and Forecasting of Temperature Based on Temporal Fusion Transformer Model: A Case Study of Urumqi
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Accurate temperature forecasting is important in many fields such as environmental engineering, disaster prevention and monitoring. This study aims to use the TFT model to predict the daily maximum, minimum and average air temperatures in Urumqi city. It was trained and optimized based on the screened and integrated temperature datasets collected from public databases such as CBE Clima, Weather Spark, and NOAA, and the performance of the TFT model in the temperature data was also investigated. Based on the MAE error criterion and the comparison between the predicted and historical true values of temperature in Urumqi city from May 4, 2024 to May 8, 2024, it is found that the TFT model can predict the short-term temperature accurately with less training set training. It is an important research step in the field of temperature analysis and prediction for finding models with better prediction performance, which will also contribute to the related decision making process.

articleTitle: Airport Crowd Counting Technology Based on Approximate Scene Initialization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Because the analysis of crowd counting requires a large number of data sets to support, and the current public data sets contain a limited number of airport images, and the data training cost in different scenarios is large, an airport crowd counting monitoring technology based on approximate scene initialization was proposed. Taking the training results initialized by kaiming on the ShanghaiTech-Part A dataset as a comparative experiment, the pre-training parameters obtained from other public datasets were initialized and tested. The experimental results show that compared with the ShanghaiTech-Part A data set using kaiming initialization and the ShanghaiTech-Part B data set pre-training model initialization, the average test error is reduced from 100.24 to 85.41, which effectively improves the counting accuracy. The self-built data set selected three similar scenes of arrival hall, waiting area and departure area from each crowd-intensive area of the airport. The experimental results show that compared with kaiming initialization, the pre-training model initialization using the mixed data set of waiting area and departure hall scene has the best effect, and the average test error is reduced from 2.69 to 2.

articleTitle: A Component-Aware Chinese Font Generation Method Based on Multi-Scale Features
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: AI-assisted generation technology for Chinese characters can significantly improve the efficiency of font library development for designers. However, existing algorithms still encounter errors in glyph strokes and structures, even when incorporating stroke semantics or font component information. This paper deepens the utilization of structural and positional features of Chinese character components by capturing the characteristics of these components at different scales, constraining their positional relationships, and enhancing the stability and consistency of glyph structures. By leveraging the cross-scale features associated with Chinese character components, the coherence of glyphs across various spatial and hierarchical levels is reinforced, improving the expression of local features. This study conducts ablation experiments on a dataset comprising 20 Chinese character libraries and compares the results with CycleGAN, Zi2zi, MX-Font, and DG-Font. The findings indicate that the proposed method enhances both the local details and overall structure of generated glyphs, with specific evaluation metrics showing significant improvement.

articleTitle: A Efficient DNN Sparsity Framework with Data Pruning and Auxiliary Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Model compression frequently leverages model pruning, an approach aimed at minimizing neural network size without compromising performance. Prior research has demonstrated the effectiveness of iterative pruning combined with retraining in producing high-quality compressed models. To gain insights into how the training set size influences the pruned model's generalization capability, we undertake an investigation that can facilitate rapid and efficient deep model pruning. Consequently, we devise a dual-model architecture that harnesses the synergy between two models to carry out simultaneous model pruning and coreset selection. Specifically, model pruning guided by an entropy-based criterion is adopted within this framework. The primary model is tasked with creating a pruned version and generating signals for selecting a retraining subset. Meanwhile, the secondary model plays a dual role: it provides supervisory signals via knowledge distillation to aid in training the primary model and offers subset selection insights during the final fine-tuning phase. We evaluate our approach using two popular backbone networks, namely ResNet and Swin Transformer, across two benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet. The outcomes validate that our framework successfully prunes a dense model while preserving the accuracy of the resultant pruned model.

articleTitle: Key Technologies for Enhancing the Communication Performance of Anti-Misoperation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: The smart power grid has emerged as a prevailing trend in the development of power systems both domestically and internationally. As a crucial component of the smart power grid, intelligent substations are currently undergoing rapid advancements. The transition of substations towards unmanned operations and intelligent management is essential to prevent operational errors that could lead to safety incidents involving personnel and equipment. The anti-misoperation device is an electrical interlock mechanism designed to prevent erroneous operations. As an indispensable component within power systems, it plays a dual role in controlling and protecting the safe and stable operation of both the grid and its loads. In transformer substations, it has become an effective preventive measure against erroneous operation accidents. The device is used in conjunction with the computer key. It not only fulfills the functional requirement of charging the computer key but also facilitates communication between the computer key and the five-defense host. The adoption of network communication facilitates more convenient connections and debugging processes. The use of a Real-Time Operating System ensures relatively high real-time performance. Network communication is implemented using the lightweight LwIP protocol. However, due to environmental factors, occasional anomalies in network communication may occur, leading to interruptions in the communication between the computer key and the five-defense host.

Author Keywords: error message statistics and packet management

articleTitle: Research on Multimodal Data Fusion Based on Optimal Adaptive Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low accuracy and poor robustness of existing multimodal data fusion models, this paper proposes a multimodal data fusion model based on adaptive coding. The model maps different modal data into the same subspace through LSTM, and adaptively learns the weights of different modal data, which helps the model to more accurately use the information of each modal data. To fully explore the interaction information among multimodal data and improve the accuracy of the model by extracting consistency and complementary features from multimodal data using a Transformer-based encoder. The uncertainty of the prediction distribution is quantified by an improved loss function to improve the anti-interference ability of the model. Experimentally evaluated on two publicly available datasets, CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI, the results show that the model performs better.

articleTitle: Fire and Smoke Detection Method in Diverse Scenarios Based on YOLOv8-FD
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Targeting the challenges of insufficient accuracy, missed detections, false detections, and single scene in existing fire smoke detection, an enhanced YOLOv8 fire smoke detection method is suggested in diversified scenarios. The YOLOv8-FD model was proposed. By designing EfficientViT as the backbone network to strengthen its local feature extraction capability while maintaining the detection model's power to extract global features, more comprehensive feature content of the target of interest is obtained, solving the problem of unclear flame boundary features and efficiently improving the situation of lost and fake detections, thereby enhancing detection accuracy. A C2f_EMSC group convolution structure has been designed, which can balance the increase in parameter and computational complexity attributable to deep convolution in the Neck part of the model, and ensure more comprehensive and efficient extraction of image feature information at different levels, effectively improving the problem of long real-time response time to fires. At the same time, coupling the LSKA attention mechanism with the SPPF structure to some extent optimizes the detection difficulty problem caused by small targets in the early stage of flames, reduces computational complexity, and improves detection efficiency. Finally, the detection capability of the YOLOv8-FD pattern was validated through experiments. The experimental findings indicate that the precision of this detection approach reaches 94.2%, the mAP0.5 index reaches 95%, and the FPS can be stable at 130FPS, which can ensure the real-time recognition of fire while ensuring the accuracy of identification and reducing the occurrence of false alarms and missed positives.

articleTitle: Toward Accurate Label-Free Immune Cell Counting via Enhanced YOLOv8 with Inverted Residual Mobile Blocks and Mixed Self-Attention Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Immune cell counting plays a crucial role in biomedical research and clinical diagnostics, particularly in assessing immune responses and disease states. However, due to the diversity of immune cells and the complexity of backgrounds in label-free imaging techniques, traditional counting methods struggle to accurately distinguish between individual and clustered immune cells. Although deep learning-based detection techniques have made significant progress, accurately identifying and counting these cells in label-free images remains challenging. To address this issue, we propose an enhanced YOLOv8 architecture, called the cell localization network (CL-YOLO), which focuses on counting immune cells in label-free imaging. Specifically, we introduce the inverted residual mobile block (iRMB) module to effectively handle complex and blurred backgrounds by extracting subtle cellular features, thereby improving the recognition accuracy of both individual and clustered cells. To solve the problem of distinguishing smaller clustered cells from individual cells and reduce false negatives, we incorporate the mixed self-attention and convolution (ACmix) module. Moreover, we validated our approach on our label-free immune cell lifecycle dataset (LICL-Dataset). The results demonstrate that CL-YOLO outperforms YOLOv8, with improvements in precision, recall, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.5-0.95, including a notable 5.3% increase in mAP@0.5, verifying its effectiveness in enhancing performance in label-free immune cell counting.

articleTitle: Multi-Hop Financial Knowledge Question-Answering Model Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: To address the urgent digitalization and intelligence needs in enterprise finance, businesses require significant improvements in information retrieval and question-answering system performance in the financial domain. This study introduces an innovative knowledge-based question-answering model for financial intelligence, which leverages a knowledge graph to enhance system performance. The proposed approach integrates relational path reasoning techniques to uncover the deep logical structure of the knowledge graph, applies knowledge graph embedding to capture extensive semantic information, and incorporates a candidate answer scoring mechanism to ensure answer accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that in multihop question-answering scenarios within the financial field, the model effectively analyzes complex queries, offering improved accuracy and faster response times, thus addressing the pressing demands of intelligent financial development for enterprises.

articleTitle: Research on QoE-Driven Panoramic Video Bit Rate Selection Strategy Under Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Panoramic video has received widespread attention because of its immersive experience it brings to users. However, panoramic video faces many technical challenges such as high bit rate, low transmission delay, and device heterogeneity. As an effective network model, mobile edge computing can provide low transmission delay and large-scale computing for panoramic videos. This paper studies the problem of downshifting panoramic video bit rate allocation in a single-edge multi-user scenario, and how to select appropriate bit rates for users to achieve the best QoE for all users under time-varying network fluctuations and edge server resource constraints. This problem is a long-term stochastic optimization problem and is difficult to solve. This paper proposes a QoE-driven panoramic video bit rate selection algorithm (PBSA), uses Lyapunov optimization technology to transform the problem into an exact optimization problem for a single time slice, and constructs Lyapunov drift plus penalty according to the resource constraints of the edge server within each time slice. function to make the best bit rate download decision. Experimental results show that under the condition of limited edge server resources, the proposed QoE-driven panoramic video bit rate selection algorithm can improve the overall user experience quality and provide smooth video playback.

articleTitle: Task Assignment Algorithm Based on Improved MADDPG
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Currently, Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USV) swarm applications have achieved certain results, and task assignment is the key part for guiding coordinated operations of the USV swarm. But there are still issues such as slow assignment plan generation speed and difficulty in dealing with emergencies in the task process of USV swarms under complex sea conditions. In response to the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes an improved Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient(MADDPG) algorithm for dynamic task assignment of USV. Specifically, based on the standard MADDPG algorithm, a feature extraction and an information fusion module are designed, and a multi-output structure for the Actor network is designed to enhance the real-time strategy generation of the algorithm in complex maritime task assignment. At the same time, an adaptive adjustment mechanism based on the evaluation network is designed, enabling the task assignment algorithm to respond quickly to emergencies and cope with real-time situation changes in the task procedure. Finally, the simulations with reasonable scenarios are conducted to verify the proposed algorithm. We also compared with the performance of our method with those of the standard MADDPG algorithm and decision tree algorithm. The simulation results show that the improved MADDPG algorithm has a faster convergence rate and smaller fluctuations after convergence, which can effectively solve the problem of task assignment for USV swarms.

articleTitle: Identification of High-Potential Technology Opportunities in Integrated Circuits from the Perspective of High-Quality Outlier Patents
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: This paper focuses on identifying high-potential technology opportunities in the field of integrated circuits through patent analysis. The research methodology combines outlier patent screening and high-quality patent evaluation techniques. Using natural language processing, outlier patents are screened, and high-quality patents within the outliers are evaluated using the entropy weight method and Pareto optimization. The subject words in these high-quality patents are then identified as highpotential technological opportunities. The study analyzes patent data from 2016–2020 and successfully verifies the effectiveness of the method. It also identifies future high-potential technology opportunities from patent data from 2021–2023. The paper acknowledges limitations, such as the lack of comprehensive quality evaluation indexes due to database limitations and the inability to accurately obtain data for certain meaningful indexes. Additionally, there is a need for a deeper understanding of the technology in the integrated circuits field to recognize corresponding technological opportunities from subject terms. Overall, this approach offers an objective and effective way to identify high-potential technology opportunities in the field of integrated circuits using patent data.

articleTitle: Research on the Medication Rules of Ancient and Modern Prescriptions for the Treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: To investigate how chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is treated using traditional Chinese medicine's drug guidelines. By organizing medical records from the past and present,a database was established, and SPSS and Python were used to perform drug frequency, nature, taste, meridians and efficacy statistics. Data mining was performed in combination with association rules, clustering and complex network analysis. A total of 837 medical records from 161 ancient books and documents were included, involving 629 prescriptions and 667 Chinese medicines, with a total frequency of use of 7314 times. High-frequency drugs include Liquorice Root, Semen Armeniacae Amarum, Cortex Cinnamomi, ginseng, Rhizoma Rhizoma Pinelliaee, Pericarpium Citri Reticulatae, Ephedra, and Cortex Mori. The medications' meridians are primarily lung meridians, their characteristics are primarily warm and neutral, and their flavor is primarily pungent and bitter. Intestinal moisture and constipation relief, heat removal and detoxification, drying dampness and phlegm resolution, expectorant, and coughing are the main effects. Association rule analysis found that core drug pairs such as Ephedra→Liquorice Root, Ephedra→Semen Armeniacae Amarum, etc. Cluster analysis divided the top 30 high-frequency drugs into four categories, and complex network analysis screened out the core formula, which included Liquorice Root, Cortex Cinnamomi, Semen Armeniacae Amarum, ginseng, Rhizoma Rhizoma Pinelliaee, Ephedra, and Pericarpium Citri Reticulatae. The goal of TCM treatment for COPD is to address the underlying cause as well as its symptoms. The core formula is centered on Liquorice Root, and treatment can be based on the patient's symptoms.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Molecular Pumps with Transformer-Based Deep Learning Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Molecular pumps are critical components in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak facility, and accurately predicting their Remaining Useful Life is essential for optimizing maintenance planning and experiment scheduling. However, precise Remaining Useful Life prediction remains challenging due to the complex operating environment and inherent data noise. To enhance prediction accuracy and model robustness, this study proposes an innovative C-Transformer hybrid model. This novel approach combines the local feature extraction capabilities of Convolution Neural Networks with the global dependency capturing abilities of Transformers, rendering it more effective in processing time series data. Using molecular pump fault data for verification demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed method in predicting the remaining service life, achieving root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) scores of 583 seconds and 501 seconds, respectively. These results significantly outperform other comparative methods. This approach not only provides a reliable Remaining Useful Life prediction solution for molecular pumps in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak facility's vacuum system but also offers valuable insights for developing predictive maintenance strategies in other complex industrial systems. By implementing this method, it is possible to prevent irreversible damage caused by prolonged overload operation, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance overall operational efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Chinese Named Entity Recognition with Integrated Channel Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
abstract: Using an Iterated Dilated Convolutional Neural Network (IDCNN) in Chinese Named Entity Recognition (NER) helps capture local information. However, the contribution of information from different positions in a sentence to the judgment of the current position is not uniform, which needs to be considered when expanding a Dilated Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN). To address this, this paper incorporates Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) into DCNN and constructs the It-erated Dilated Convolutional Attention Network (IDCAN). The model focuses on the importance of different channel information and integrates the Linguistically-motivated Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformers (LERT), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), and Conditional Random Fields (CRF) to form a Chinese NER model. The model uses LERT for word vector construction, BiGRU for capturing temporal features, IDCAN for extracting key local features, and CRF for feature decoding. On the Daily, MSRA and E-commerce Chinese datasets, the model achieved F1 scores of 96.88%, 95.15% and 90.52%, respectively, outperforming other models.
